title: BRIDGING FAIRNESS AND EXPLAINABILITY: CAN INPUT-BASED EXPLANATIONS PROMOTE FAIRNESS IN HATE SPEECH DETECTION?
findings: The paper's findings on using input-based explanations for fairness generally apply to religion alongside race and gender. Explanations were effective for detecting biased predictions and mitigating bias during training in religious contexts. However, they proved unreliable for automatically selecting fair models. The degree of bias and the effectiveness of mitigation techniques varied between datasets, with religion bias being the most successfully mitigated category on the Jigsaw dataset.
